title: Receiver contract
description: What one destination kind requires of a request, and how it answers when it accepts or refuses one. The behaviours every kind shares are in receivers/modes.json. See README.md in this folder.

kind.description: The destination kind, as in the catalog

model.description: lab: what the fake receiver checks today. confirmed: checked against the CRM's sandbox (RFC-006)

requires.description: Fields that must be present and not blank. A dotted path into a JSON body (inbox_lead.from_first), name[key] for an array of {name, value}, or a form field name. May be empty (a plain webhook requires nothing by itself); a lab receiver URL's ?require=A,B adds fields on top, and a scenario states those with the answer's 'requires'

from.description: Which part of the standard lead fills it

refusesMissing.description: The answer when a required field is missing or blank

duplicates.description: How this kind handles a lead it may have seen, which decides what follows an unknown outcome (RFC-008 §4.3). idempotency-key: ignores a request with a key it has seen. lookup: we can ask whether a record with our lead reference exists. external-reference: stores our reference but does not deduplicate. none: no way to tell. harmless: a second copy costs nothing. 'none' until confirmed

toConfirm.description: What the sandbox must still settle
